title: Modern C# Features & Source Generators
description: Master records, pattern matching enhancements, source generators, and functional-style programming in modern C#.

data.text: Records (C# 9+) provide a concise syntax for immutable data types with built-in equality comparison, deconstruction, and with-expressions for non-destructive mutation. They're ideal for DTOs, value objects, and domain models.

data.title: Records vs Classes
Record Structs
data.text: Use record struct for value-type records that should be stack-allocated. Use record for reference-type records. Record structs are great for small, immutable data like coordinates or measurements.
C# has progressively enhanced pattern matching with relational patterns, logical patterns, list patterns, and property patterns. These enable expressive, declarative code.

data.title: Modern Pattern Matching

data.text: Source generators (C# 9+) compile code that generates additional source files during build. They're used for reducing boilerplate, improving performance, and implementing compile-time metaprogramming.

data.title: Implementing a Simple Source Generator
Popular Source Generator Libraries
data.text: CommunityToolkit.Mvvm, Mapperly, StronglyTypedId, and Scrutor use source generators to reduce boilerplate. Consider using these before writing your own generators.
Modern C# supports functional programming patterns with immutability, expression-bodied members, local functions, and declarative code. These patterns reduce bugs and improve readability.

data.title: Functional-Style Code

cards.title: File-Scoped Namespaces
cards.description: Use namespace MyNamespace; instead of nesting braces. Reduces indentation.
cons: Cannot have multiple namespaces in file

cards.title: Required Members
cards.description: Mark properties as required to enforce initialization via object initializer.

cards.title: Primary Constructors
cards.description: Define constructor parameters directly on class/record declaration.

data.title: Modern Syntax Examples
Key Takeaways
points: Records provide immutable data types with value-based equality and minimal boilerplate
Pattern matching enables expressive, declarative code with relational, logical, and list patterns
Source generators compile code that generates additional source files during build
Use source generators to reduce boilerplate (e.g., INotifyPropertyChanged, mappers)
Functional-style C# uses immutability, expression-bodied members, and local functions
File-scoped namespaces reduce nesting and improve readability
Required members enforce initialization at compile time
Primary constructors reduce boilerplate in class and record definitions
data.takeaway: Modern C# features enable cleaner, more expressive code with less boilerplate. Records, pattern matching, and source generators are particularly powerful for reducing repetitive code while maintaining type safety and performance.
